name: Ramesh Raskar
why: MIT Media Lab (Camera Culture) professor and projector-AR pioneer (Shader Lamps, iLamps, RFIG Lamps with Johnny Lee); RFIG video exists at youtube.com/watch?v=MURwa1lWDsY.

name: Karen X Cheng
why: Director and creative technologist known for viral camera, AR and AI video tricks; co-made the Spectacles 3 butterfly film with Clara Bacou.

name: PHORIA (Ben Ferns)
why: Melbourne XR studio that co-built the WebXR mixed-reality showcase Spatial Fusion with Lusion and Meta; Ben Ferns posts WebXR tech walkthroughs.

name: Yi-Wen Lin
why: London-based Taiwanese creative coder (WENSDAY) who co-made the AR Virtual Plants demo with Matt DesLauriers; WebGL/AR sketches.

name: Hamill Industries (Pablo Barquín & Anna Diaz)
why: Barcelona visual studio mixing robotics, real-time graphics and computer vision; built the AI dance ensemble Engendered Otherness and CORTEX's live scenography with Kianí del Valle, plus robot-camera live shows for Floating Points.

name: Alberto Novello (JesterN)
why: Sound artist and EEG hacker who wrote the brainwave-to-laser system of (UN)FOCUSSED and made the brain-controlled performance Fragmentation.

name: Andrej Boleslavský (id144)
why: Interactive artist and Mária Júdová's long-time collaborator on Camouflage, body(input); and Everywhen; also made interactive particle installations such as Flow at Signal Festival.

name: Yago de Quay
why: Musician-dancer who performs with Kinect-tracked movement driving music and visuals (Dance Jockey, Breakdown with visiophone).

name: Choy Ka Fai
why: Singapore-born Berlin artist working on dance, motion capture and trance; co-directed the VR piece Constellation of the Flesh with Mária Júdová.

name: The Sancho Plan (Ed Cookson)
why: Bristol audiovisual group behind Big Screen Augmented Reality (2010) and live AR music performances with animated characters; only the big-screen piece was added here (under Neil Mendoza).

name: Oriol Ferrer Mesià
why: openFrameworks developer (ex-Snibbe Interactive) whose Benetton window installations include camera mirrors such as Elastic Mirror, TimeLoop and Kaleidoscope.

name: Tangible Interaction
why: Vancouver studio behind the openFrameworks Digital Graffiti Wall (2010 Olympics) and early marker AR such as AR Hippo for TELUS; mostly commercial, needs a careful pick.

name: Parag K. Mital
why: Artist-researcher whose 'Memory' (2010, with Agelos Papadakis) augments hanging glass sculptures with projected faces; also real-time audiovisual resynthesis mirrors.

name: Champagne Valentine (with Aaron Meyers)
why: Amsterdam studio that made early webcam AR musical instruments (2010) and interactive shop-window mirrors with openFrameworks developer Aaron Meyers.

name: Patrick Baudisch
why: HPI Potsdam professor behind Imaginary Reality Gaming, Imaginary Phone and many body-scale interaction prototypes (Holz's PhD advisor).

name: Andreas Fender
why: First author of Causality-preserving Asynchronous Reality and InfinitePaint (ETH Zurich); mixed-reality work on time and physical causality.

name: Lung-Pan Cheng
why: Lead author of Reality Rifts; known for TurkDeck and Haptic Turk (people as haptic props for VR); National Taiwan University.

name: Mohamed Kari
why: First author of TransforMR and SoundsRide (Porsche / ETH Zurich); mixed reality that re-skins the street and the car ride.

name: Philip Schuette
why: Dutch artist behind playful interactive installations SUN (a bouncy ball moves the sun) and BODY (your pose as an image search) with Random Studio.

name: Nick Verstand
why: Dutch audiovisual artist, co-creator of ANIMA with onformative; makes light-and-sound installations that respond to visitors.

name: Matt Clugston
why: Creative director and motion-graphics artist behind the real-time mocap imagery in Holosphere's Waterhall performance and the University of Birmingham projection show.

name: Job van Nuenen
why: Built the interactive framework and sound for Children of the Light's ZEROTIME, where visitors' phone torches are turned into a live soundscape.

name: Stuart Batchelor
why: Computer artist who co-created the participatory shemza.digital painting apps and installations with Aphra Shemza.

name: Marek Simonik (Record3D)
why: Record3D app author; open Unity VFX Graph demos stream iPhone LiDAR/TrueDepth point clouds live into VFX Graph (no own demo video found).

name: Dan Miller
why: Unity AR evangelist; open ARFoundation_VFX and ARBodyTrackingVFX repos (AR Foundation + VFX Graph); videos likely on X @DanMillerDev.

name: Saki Komikado (komietty)
why: Geometry programmer; open Unity moxi ink painting, CIP fluid, bitonic-sort SPH and vector-field repos; videos likely on X.

name: Masatatsu Nakamura (mattatz)
why: Open Unity CellularGrowth, Dendrite, voxelizer, procedural tree/flower and volume rendering repos; demo videos mostly GIF/X.

name: Cyanilux
why: Shader Graph artist with open URP repos (retro CRT, watercolour, custom lighting); showcase videos on X.

name: Roel Kok
why: Kinect-VFX-Graph (213 stars): Kinect depth feed into Unity VFX Graph; needs a playable video.

name: Codrin-Mihail (Kodrin)
why: Open VFX-Essentials HDRP workshop and GPU-FlowField compute-shader particle repos.

name: Angela He (zephyo)
why: 2D-Unity-Experiments (279 stars): URP/Shader Graph visual experiments; videos likely on X @zephybite.

name: Aras Pranckevičius
why: Graphics engineer (ex-Unity) whose open-source UnityGaussianSplatting renders 3D Gaussian Splatting scenes in Unity; Keijiro's SplatVFX README recommends it as the more complete implementation.

name: Ronald van Wijnen
why: Author of spectral.js, an open-source Kubelka-Munk pigment color-mixing library with web demos; Keijiro ported it to Unity for Fluo and his pigment fluid-art tests.

name: FMS_Cat (0b5vr)
why: Demoscene and WebGL real-time visuals artist who performed alongside Keijiro at Channel and Liquidroom; publishes source code.

name: AMAGI (fand)
why: Web graphics artist behind vfx-js and VEDA live-coding tools; active in the same Tokyo live-coding scene.

name: kaiware007
why: Unity VJ shader developer (reaction-diffusion, hex tiling, VJ shader talks) with public repos.
